scope: Independent read-only audit of final local raw files; no remote calls or reruns; this JSON is the sole audit write.
checks: Both hosts runtime files match finalized SHA manifest; binary/source/dependency and 31-pass Linux client receipts match.
Eight formal points and eighteen successful phases; exactly two namespace loads and no extra load directory.
All phase reply counts match raw INFO commandstats with zero failed/rejected calls; paired metrics have complete equal counts.
Full state bytes match between phases/versions; unchanged ZINCRBY state, ZREM/ZADD parity, inactive flags, bounded full-member samples and final state files pass.
Actual empty recovery and clean checkpoints 1 through 8 are confirmed in original server logs; final checkpoint has 16384 entries.
Compact transaction counts are zero throughout; grouped transactions are positive and equal one per modifying command during warm/formal.
All sixteen CPU/NIC observations have 46 stable-identity samples over forty-five seconds; zero read errors and selected-NIC errors/drops. All eight server logs have no warning/error records.
interpretation_notes: Measured candidate revision remains 32bdd6b. Later comment-only revision 001442e8 was not measured.

Fixed main-then-candidate order; scores, member replacement flags and physical storage state evolve continuously. These are one-run observations, not randomized independent resets or isolated causal effect estimates.

Specific compact comparison confound: main compact runs before the grouped namespace is loaded (8192 total keys), whereas candidate compact runs after both namespaces exist (16384 total keys, including 8 GiB of grouped logical member payload). Commands still target only their own namespace, but the total resident/storage background is not identical, so the -5.58% and -3.22% compact differences cannot be labeled isolated code regressions.

Candidate grouped ZINCRBY is nonstationary: formal ten-second means are 38321.0, 36691.6, 35864.2, 35460.7, 27381.7, 26859.4 ops/s. The +28.24% is the full fixed-window aggregate, not a stable improvement.

Candidate grouped ZINCRBY warm last twenty seconds are 25920.4 and 29763.6 ops/s, followed by the formal first ten seconds at 38321.0. A slowdown was already present late in warmup and recurs in the formal window; ninety seconds of warmup did not establish a stable rate.

Monitor bins use their own timestamps and record approximate controller-relative bounds. The client operation buckets start at its internal monotonic barrier, whose absolute timestamp is not exported; exact subsecond alignment cannot be proved from these files.

During candidate grouped ZINCRBY, server CPU stays about 13.07 to 12.53 cores while client CPU falls about 0.65 to 0.43 cores. There are no NIC errors/drops or TCP retransmissions in that observation. Aggregate client CPU is low and NIC rates are far below the previously measured network capacity; no evident network-loss or client-CPU-saturation event explains the drop.

Background counters are only available at phase boundaries. Main/candidate formal cleaner rounds are 1023/1120 and retired blocks 5138/5282; failures and commit-backpressure waits are zero, queue endpoints drained. These confirm background work occurs but cannot associate a specific cleaner or defrag episode with the forty-second rate drop. Logs have no corresponding timestamped background event.
Server CPU includes polling, and Linux process IO counters do not account for SPDK device IO. Do not infer device idleness or a specific CPU/storage bottleneck from these counters.

nonstationarity_detail.description: Warm decline becomes clear around client second 67; formal decline becomes clear around second 42-43. Monitor client/server NIC rates fall concurrently, without recorded NIC loss or host-wide TCP retransmissions. Server process CPU falls only modestly. Snapshot-only background counters and untraced SPDK IO cannot resolve which server-side activity causes the slowdown.
nonstationarity_detail.background_sampling_limit: No per-second transaction/cleaner/defrag telemetry and no warm CPU/NIC monitor were recorded; boundary counters cannot be aligned to ten-second rate buckets. CPU/NIC formal intervals record controller-relative wall-clock bounds; exact internal client bucket start is not exported.
